v1.feedback: The ochre palette shift is genuine and well-graded (yellow ochre → raw sienna → burnt umber), and the settling dust layer at the base sells the earth-pigment concept. The burst system still reads a bit too pyrotechnic — slow its initial velocity further and widen the cone so bursts feel like thrown pigment powder rather than firework remnants with recolored uniforms. Consider adding a faint horizontal banding or sedimentary striation to the tower particles (modulate alpha by quantized height bands) to reinforce the geological/archaeological register the comments promise but the shader doesn't yet deliver.

v2.feedback: The ochre palette genuinely transforms the parent tower — yellow ochre→raw sienna→burnt umber reads as geological time passing through the form, and the sedimentary strata concept is a smart structural addition. However, the strata bands are too subtle: the triangle-wave modulation floors at 0.55 alpha, so bands barely register against the additive glow — drop the floor to ~0.2 and widen the dark gaps so the cross-section layering reads at a glance. The pigment-throw clouds should drift more decisively sideways with visible arc trajectories to sell the Lascaux hand-cast gesture rather than generic ambient particles.
